entries.subject: Hui et al. (2020) nucleus radius estimate
entries.finding: Most likely at most 0.4 km from the non-gravitational acceleration and CO production at assumed density 0.5 g/cm³; used as a 0.4 km display sphere.

entries.subject: Jewitt et al. (2020) Hubble nucleus bounds
entries.finding: Coma modelling limits the radius to at most 0.5 km (albedo 0.04); the acceleration requires at least 0.2 km (density 500 kg/m³). Recorded as the bounds around the display size.

entries.subject: Kim et al. (2020) rotation pole
entries.finding: Pole RA 205°, Dec 52° (obliquity 30°) from coma anisotropy; the prime meridian, spin phase and period stay undetermined.

entries.subject: 2020 outburst and splitting
entries.finding: Hubble saw outbursts and a fragment in March 2020; fragment sizes and positions are not modelled on the single display nucleus.
entries.revisitWhen: A fragment size and trajectory solution is published.

entries.subject: Coma photographs, artist impressions and coma colour as surface data
entries.finding: Every image shows an unresolved nucleus inside its coma, and published colours measure the coma; none maps or colours the nucleus surface.
entries.revisitWhen: Resolved imaging or a nucleus colour is published.

entries.subject: JPL Horizons fixed-epoch trajectory
entries.finding: Horizons 2I (C/2019 Q4) elements and independent vectors at the 2026-09-03 scene epoch: eccentricity 3.35 at 48.10 au. Two-body propagation differs from Horizons by 528 km and 522 km 30 days either side.
